conclusion: Safe Rust methods cannot be invoked through a nil Chunk reference, accepted FieldType.EvalType always returns one of the handled evaluation classes, and ETReal arises only from FLOAT or DOUBLE; the four listed branches therefore have no typed Rust or accepted valid-input entry path.
entry_surface: Chunk methods require an existing &Chunk, while both accepted Go and Rust FieldType evaluation exhaustively map every type code and restrict real evaluation to FLOAT and DOUBLE.
proof_steps: Confirmed the two Go branches require a nil method receiver and that Rust exposes Capacity and MemoryUsage only through a non-null shared reference.
Confirmed accepted parser FieldType.EvalType maps every type byte to a handled evaluation class, with FLOAT and DOUBLE as the only ETReal sources, and Rust preserves the same exhaustive mapping.
